findings.evidence: admin/scratch/003-complete-skill-develop/lane-assignments.json:tasks[8] (T9) lane_reason — 'verifiability=high (binary: literal sentinel chat line; refusal exits without writing; `superseded_by_retro: true` is the single-boolean signal per Gate 3 revision goal-r1-f2)'. Cross-referencing 003-complete-skill-tasks.md:T9 acceptance: 'When `/specflow:complete {task-id}` is invoked WITHOUT the `--amend` flag AND the existing `task-history.json` entry for `{task-id}` has `superseded_by_retro: true`...' AND T4 acceptance: 'a `specflow:complete` run that finds the field absent from the existing entry refuses with the literal sentinel...' The lane plan binds T9's binary signal to `superseded_by_retro: true`, but the field's existence depends on `specflow:develop` Phase F.5 emitting `superseded_by_retro: false` as the default flag in its initial write — a cross-skill prerequisite per T4's Notes-line. The lane plan does not name the unstated assumption that on the FIRST `specflow:complete` v1 run (against a `task-history.json` entry written by a Phase F.5 that has NOT yet shipped the `superseded_by_retro: false` default), T9's existence-check operates on an entry where the field is structurally absent — which is T4's runtime-refusal path, not T9's plain-mode-refusal path. The lane plan treats T9 as wholly Green on the assumption the cross-skill prerequisite has landed, but that's an unstated dependency.
findings.claim: Unstated load-bearing assumption — T9's lane reasoning binds verifiability=high to `superseded_by_retro: true` as a single-boolean signal, but the field's existence on the existing task-history.json entry depends on a cross-skill prerequisite (specflow:develop Phase F.5 emitting `superseded_by_retro: false` as default) that the PRD R4 names as out-of-scope-for-this-skill and routes to a separate `specflow:develop` enhancement PRD. The lane plan does not surface this as a sequencing dependency in T9's `depends_on` field — T9 lists `[T3, T4]` as upstream, but the `specflow:develop` enhancement PRD itself is not a task in this feature, so T9's Green-lane execution assumes the prerequisite has landed independently. Think-Before-Coding principle: 'Name unstated assumptions in the artefact, not silently in the implementer's head.' The plan as written hides the (T9's Green-lane verifiability) ↔ (cross-skill prerequisite landed) dependency.
findings.proposed_change: Either (a) add a `depends_on_external` field to T9's lane-assignments.json entry citing the `specflow:develop` enhancement PRD (e.g. `depends_on_external: ['specflow:develop-enhancement-superseded-by-retro-default']`) so the cross-skill prerequisite is explicit in the lane plan, OR (b) extend T9's `lane_reason` text with a clause naming the prerequisite: 'Verifiability=high ASSUMING `specflow:develop` Phase F.5 emits `superseded_by_retro: false` default; if the prerequisite has not landed at execution time, T4's runtime refusal fires and T9 never reaches its existence-check path.' Option (a) is more structurally explicit; option (b) preserves the lane plan's per-task entry shape and surfaces the assumption as prose. Either resolves the unstated assumption.
